correctness.rationale: The Frobenius loss is a strictly convex quadratic in squared positive diagonal factors because its Hessian Schur complement is 1-rho^4/d>0; its unique stationary point has positive explicit coordinates. Extremal eigenvectors of the original star have identical squared coordinates and thus yield a universal condition lower bound with only scalar equality. The exact 2x2 invariant block gives the full spectrum and, as epsilon=1-rho^2 tends to zero, a~d epsilon/(d-1), b->1, lambda_minus~d epsilon^2/(d-1), lambda_plus->1, proving the exact (d-1)/(16d) coefficient relative to kappa(A)^2. Exact algebra and 6440 finite formula cross-checks agreed; finite tests are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The same squared Frobenius congruence objective is an explicit operational baseline in the motivating numerical preconditioning literature. This exact positive-definite family, starting from a condition-optimal diagonal scaling, yields an unbounded and quadratically growing condition penalty while the optimized Frobenius objective improves, exposing structural limitations of an algebraic surrogate. A globally solved optimizer, a dimension-three minimal obstruction, and sharp asymptotic constant give a reproducible benchmark beyond a routine estimate; no runtime/iteration claim is made.
